summary: Published node2's port-8080 HTTP service through node1's management address on TCP/80, keeping the service on the private link, and completed the mandatory sequential restart/recovery proof on all three nodes.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1 (OpenWrt) has br-lan/eth0 as the shared management network (10.100.165.0/24) with node2 and node3, plus an unused eth1; node2 (CentOS) has enp1s0 on the management network and enp8s0 unconfigured (the private link to node1's eth1); node3 has only the management NIC.
Brought up the private link: static 192.168.50.1/24 on node1 eth1 (new UCI interface 'priv') and 192.168.50.2/24 on node2 enp8s0 via nmcli; verified reachability with ping.
Deployed a demo HTTP service on node2 as a systemd unit (demo-http.service, python3 http.server) bound explicitly to 192.168.50.2:8080 only, and opened 8080/tcp in firewalld.

On node1: created firewall zone 'priv' (network=priv, masq=1) so DNAT'd flows get source-NATed to node1's private IP, avoiding asymmetric routing since node2 and node3 share the management subnet; added a lan-to-priv forwarding rule and a redirect (DNAT) rule mapping lan:80 to 192.168.50.2:8080; committed UCI and reloaded firewall.

Verified end-to-end: node3 curl to http://10.100.165.10:80/ returns the node2 service response (HTTP 200); direct node3 access to node2's management IP:8080 and to the private IP:8080 both fail, confirming the service stays private and reachable only via node1's publish path.

Captured boot_id and health baseline on all 3 nodes, then restarted node1, node2, and node3 sequentially (one at a time) with each OS's native reboot, polled exec availability until each returned, confirmed a changed boot_id on each, and re-verified private-link config, service health, and the full node3-to-node1:80-to-node2:8080 path after every single restart before moving to the next node.

evidence.requirement: Baseline topology and service state before changes
evidence.summary: ip/uci/ss output established node1 eth1 and node2 enp8s0 as the unconfigured private link, and that no HTTP service yet existed on node2 (port 8080 not listening).

evidence.requirement: Private network established between node1 and node2 (eth1<->enp8s0), excluding node3
evidence.summary: Static IPs 192.168.50.1/2 assigned on node1 eth1 / node2 enp8s0; ping confirms L2/L3 reachability on the private link.

evidence.requirement: HTTP service on node2 port 8080, private-network only
evidence.summary: systemd service demo-http.service listens only on 192.168.50.2:8080 (not 0.0.0.0); node1 fetch over the private link succeeds.

evidence.requirement: Service published via node1 management IP on TCP 80, reachable from node3
evidence.summary: UCI firewall zone/forwarding/DNAT redirect committed on node1; node3 curl to http://10.100.165.10:80/ returns the node2 service body with HTTP 200; nft ruleset shows the DNAT rule with a packet hit.

evidence.requirement: Service stays on the private network (not directly exposed to node3)
evidence.summary: node3 direct curl to node2's management IP:8080 and to the private IP:8080 both fail (000/refused), proving the service is unreachable except through node1's publish path.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id e7fce50c captured; reboot acked and returned before disconnect; subsequent probe timed out then succeeded; new boot_id df8dec85 confirmed; UCI config, firewall redirect, and full node3->node1->node2 path verified healthy post-restart.

evidence.requirement: Node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 2c237d4f captured; systemctl reboot acked; probes timed out/reset then succeeded; new boot_id 02d267b6 confirmed; private IP, demo-http.service, firewalld port, and full publish path verified healthy post-restart.

evidence.requirement: Node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5b620f5a captured; systemctl reboot acked; probes timed out/reset then succeeded; new boot_id ee9fa2d1 confirmed; post-restart node3 successfully re-fetched the service via node1:80 while direct access to node2 remained blocked.
